title: Coherent derived Hom for bounded-above and bounded-below algebraic complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $K,L\in D(A)$, the ordinary module derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that every $H^j(K)$ and $H^j(L)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and that there exist integers $u,v$ such that $H^j(K)=0$ for $j>u$ and $H^j(L)=0$ for $j<v$. Then every cohomology module of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$ is finitely generated, and $H^r(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L))=0$ for $r<v-u$. Here $R\operatorname{Hom}_A$ is the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site with coefficient ring $A$.

source.place: Tag 0D0C, lemma-coherent-internal-hom, proof: the explicitly stated algebra problem for L in D^+_Coh(A) and K in D^-_Coh(A), with its lower bound v-u from the displayed bounded spectral sequences.

proof.text: We will use the following elementary finite-generation argument over the given Noetherian ring $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], a submodule of a finite $A$-module is finite. A quotient is finite because the images of any finite generating set generate it [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Thus subquotients are finite. If $0\to B\to C\to D\to0$ is exact with $B,D$ finite, choose generators of $B$ and lifts in $C$ of generators of $D$; their union generates $C$, since subtracting a linear combination of the lifts leaves an element of $B$. Induction on the number of successive quotients now shows that a module with a finite filtration and finite successive quotients is finite.

source.place: Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, with the elementary generator argument used in its proof.

proof.text: Fix the integers $u,v$ in the hypothesis and first let $N$ be any finite $A$-module placed in degree zero. Apply [lem-trf-source-hyperext-module-target] to $K,N,u$. Its $E_2$ terms are $\operatorname{Ext}^i_A(H^{-j}(K),N)$ for $i\geq0$, and are zero outside $i\geq0$, $j\geq-u$. The two module arguments are finite by the hypothesis on $K$ and our choice of $N$, and $A$ is Noetherian, so [lem-sc-ext-noetherian-finite] makes every such $E_2$ term finite. The negative $i$ terms are zero by the source-sequence statement.

source.place: Tag 0D0C, lemma-coherent-internal-hom, proof: the algebra problem and the two displayed Ext spectral sequences.

proof.text: In this spectral sequence every $E_{s+1}^{i,j}$ is a quotient of a submodule of $E_s^{i,j}$. Step 1 therefore proves by induction on $s\geq2$ that all pages have finite terms. A fixed bidegree eventually stabilizes by [lem-trf-source-hyperext-module-target], so its $E_\infty$ term is finite too; this uses eventual stabilization, not finiteness of an infinite intersection. In total degree $p$ the same node gives a finite filtration of $H^p(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,N[0]))$ with graded terms indexed by $-u\leq j\leq p$. Step 1 makes the abutment finite. This proves finite generation for every $p\in\mathbf Z$ and every finite module $N$, including the zero abutments for $p<-u$.

source.place: Tag 0D0C, lemma-coherent-internal-hom, proof: the algebra problem and the two displayed Ext spectral sequences.

proof.text:
Now apply [lem-per-bounded-above-rhom-hyperext] on the one-object site with only the identity covering, with coefficient ring $A$, and with its parameters $r=u$, $c=v$. Sheaves on this site are precisely modules, so its derived category and cohomology are the ordinary ones. Its internal Hom is exactly the $R\operatorname{Hom}_A$ in the statement: the Hom-complex/K-injective formula in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is unchanged on this site. The bounds required by that node are exactly the assumed upper bound on $K$ and lower bound on $L$. We obtain an $A$-module spectral sequence
$$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,H^q(L)[0]))\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H^{p+q}(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)),$$
zero outside $p\geq-u$, $q\geq v$, with a finite exhaustive separated abutment filtration in each total degree.

source.place: Tag 0D0C, lemma-coherent-internal-hom, proof: the algebra problem and the two displayed Ext spectral sequences.

proof.text: Each $H^q(L)$ is finite by hypothesis, so Step 3, with $N=H^q(L)$, makes every $E_2^{p,q}$ of Step 4 finite. As before, kernels are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], quotients are generated by images of generators, and induction on pages makes every term of every finite page finite. For fixed $(p,q)$ the incoming differential is zero when $s>p+u$, while the outgoing differential is zero when $s>q-v+1$, by the support bounds of [lem-per-bounded-above-rhom-hyperext]; hence $E_\infty^{p,q}$ is a finite-page term and is finite. In total degree $n$, that node supplies a finite filtration with graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$ and only $v\leq n-p\leq n+u$ contributing. Step 1 gives finite generation of $H^n(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L))$. If $n<v-u$ the interval is empty, so every graded piece is zero; a finite exhaustive separated filtration with zero graded pieces has zero abutment. This is the required vanishing and completes both conclusions.
